title: Exercise 7B · Q10
summary: Find the pole length, then use the unchanged length in the new position to find how far the foot slides.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q10: A straight pole PR is leaning against a vertical wall MQ. (i) Given that PQ = 4.2 m and RQ = 1.1 m, find the length of the pole. (ii) The upper end of the pole, P, slides down 0.9 m to a point on the wall, X. Calculate YR, the distance the lower end of the pole has slid away from its original position R.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A straight pole **PR** leans against a vertical wall **MQ**. (i) **PQ = 4.2 m**, **RQ = 1.1 m** — find the length of the pole. (ii) The top **P** slides down **0.9 m** to a point **X** on the wall. Find **YR**, how far the foot has slid from **R** to **Y**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔPQR, **∠Q = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **PR**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{RQ^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{RQ^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{4.2^2} + \role{legB}{1.1^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{17.64} + \role{legB}{1.21} \\ &= \role{hyp}{18.85}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 18.85 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{RQ^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{4.2^2} + \role{legB}{1.1^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{17.64} + \role{legB}{1.21} \\ &= \role{hyp}{18.85} \\ \role{hyp}{PR} &= \sqrt{18.85} = \role{ans}{4.34\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: (ii) Find QX
steps.narration: **P** slides down **0.9 m** to **X**, so **QX = PQ − 0.9**.\[\begin{aligned}QX &= 4.2 - 0.9 = 3.3\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: The pole length is unchanged
steps.narration: **XY** is the same pole, so **XY = PR**. Use **ΔXQY** (∠Q = 90°) to find **QY**.\[\begin{aligned}QY^2 &= XY^2 - QX^2 \\ &= 18.85 - 3.3^2 \\ &= 18.85 - 10.89 = 7.96 \\ QY &= \sqrt{7.96} = 2.82\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Find YR
steps.narration: **YR** is how far the foot slid — the difference between **QY** and **QR**.\[\begin{aligned}YR &= QY - QR \\ &= 2.82 - 1.1 = \role{ans}{1.72\ \text{m}}\ \text{(3 s.f.)}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check QX
challenges.prompt: PQ = 4.2 m and P slides down 0.9 m. Find QX.

takeaways: A sliding ladder/pole keeps the **same length** — only its angle against the wall changes.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
